subject: Edge cache residency attestation + conditional DPA routing for AsterCare
messages:
From: Alice Martin <alice.martin@astercare.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@astercare.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Residency attestation and edge cache question

Diego,

Thanks for the call this morning. Two follow-ups from our security and procurement teams: 1) We need a short residency attestation covering onshore caching behavior for PII-derived embeddings used by our pilot; 2) If Redwood uses edge caches outside the EU/UK for token-level KV caching, we need to understand the routing rules and whether a conditional DPA routing clause is available so we can keep data within our approved geographies.

Can you share a draft attestation and any proposed contract language for conditional routing (we have a narrow whitelist of countries for edge nodes)? Attaching our network/dataflow diagram for context.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement hopes to close by 12/15.

— Alice
Alice Martin
Head of Security & Privacy, AsterCare
Alice.Martin@astercare.com
Attachments: astercare-dataflow-diagram.png
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Martin <alice.martin@astercare.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency attestation and edge cache question

Alice — thanks for the clear ask and the diagram. I've looped in Kimberly (privacy/infrastructure) and Marissa (DPA owner) to document two deliverables: a one-page residency attestation template and proposed conditional routing language to add to the DPA (or as a short SOW if you prefer).

High-level answers up front: 1) Redwood can provide an attestation that token-level KV caches are ephemeral and that persistent storage for customer data (models, embeddings snapshots) is pinned by region per the DPA. 2) Edge nodes run ephemeral caching across regions to optimize latency; we support policy-based routing (region-first, then cost-tier fallback). We can add a contractual constraint to restrict cache egress to your approved country set — this is effectively a routing policy with an operational SLA and escalation path.

Next steps I propose:
- Kimberly to produce the residency attestation doc (short, signed by Privacy)
- Marissa to propose DPA redlines for conditional routing + fallback exclusions
- We'll drop both into a shared Drive folder and propose an internal review window (48 hours) so procurement can start legal review.

I'll attach a template attestation and a draft clause by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Partner Success, Redwood Inference
Attachments: none
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Martin <alice.martin@astercare.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 16:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Residency attestation and edge cache question

Alice — attaching the residency attestation template and an initial draft of conditional routing language for the DPA. Highlights:

- Attestation: short signed statement describing how Redwood persists customer content (region pinned for stored artifacts) and how KV/prefix caches are encrypted in transit, ephemeral by default (TTL <= 2 hours), and excluded from backups.
- Conditional routing clause (draft): allows Customer to specify an explicit allowed-country list for edge-cache egress; Redwood will enforce via routing policy and provide an exception path for emergency fallback with 48-hour notice + vendor approval.

Operational notes (non-contractual):
- Enforcing allowed-country lists is straightforward for our routing layer; we'll need AsterCare to provide IP ranges/ASN or a country whitelist.
- For strict onshore-only requirements (no cross-border caching at all), we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment; hosted plans can be configured but have practical limitations on edge coverage.

Please review and flag any specific legal language changes. We'll also attach a short runbook for how fallback notifications and audit trail will work.

— Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-residency-attestation-template.pdf, dpa-proposed-redlines.docx
From: Alice Martin <alice.martin@astercare.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@astercare.com, legal@astercare.com
Date: Mon, 8 Dec 2026 15:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Residency attestation and edge cache question

Kimberly / Diego — thank you, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few quick items from our side after internal review: 

1) The attestation language looks fine — legal only asked that the TTL language be explicit ("<= 2 hours for token-level KV caches") and that Redwood confirm no backups are made of cached content.
2) The conditional routing draft is mostly acceptable; legal wants the emergency fallback to require both Customer consent and a written incident justification (not unilateral Redwood action). Can Redwood add a clause capturing that requirement?
3) For procurement: can you confirm whether this routing control requires Dedicated/Private or whether Hosted customers can get the same guarantees? We may include an acceptance criterion in the SOW depending on the answer.

If possible, please update the docs with the clarifications attached and return by EOD tomorrow so we can circulate to our Legal/Procurement/Platform teams ahead of the 12/15 target.

Best,
Alice
Alice Martin
Head of Security & Privacy, AsterCare
Attachments: none
